hypothesis: Cache-level tiling with scalar i-k-j order should improve locality over the parent's r-c-k traversal: the inner j loop reads B and updates C contiguously while reusing each A value, and the bounded A/B/C tiles should reduce cache working sets for larger arbitrary n. K tiles remain ascending, preserving each output's accumulation order. This tests interchange and blocking together, not blocking in isolation from a scalar i-k-j control. It uses no packing or scratch allocation; the full output memset remains part of the call.

The baseline's output-element dot products traverse B with a row-stride. A 4-row by 16-column outer-product tile instead streams contiguous B columns, reuses each loaded B block across four output rows, and exposes independent column updates for SIMD. It retains increasing-k accumulation for each output and handles partial row and column tiles. The available baseline is correct but provides only an aggregate timing, so any throughput benefit remains a hypothesis for controller measurement.

A static OpenMP schedule over independent output rows should reduce large-matrix wall time when the supplied thread budget exceeds one, while preserving each output's k-order accumulation. Small matrices may lose time to OpenMP overhead. Initializing each output once inside the same row loop keeps initialization within the measured call and avoids a separate clear pass; the same kernel and OpenMP region structure support 1- and 4-thread comparisons.

Test the analyst's scalar i-k-j control against the original r-c-k traversal and the measured 32x64x32 blocked i-k-j candidate. This materially differs from the recent blocked mechanism: it adds no cache tiles, B packing, or scratch allocation, and isolates whether contiguous inner-j access to B and C plus reuse of one A value explains most of the locality benefit. If contiguous traversal dominates, complete-call timings should improve over r-c-k and approach the blocked result; if tiles matter, the blocked candidate should remain faster. Stop treating this control as a candidate if it fails correctness/full-C overwrite or if repeated timings show no improvement over r-c-k beyond run-to-run variation.

Compared with the measured 4x16 candidate, a 4x8 tile and one SIMD update loop for all four row accumulators should reduce live column-vector state and loop overhead while retaining B reuse. Reject on any correctness failure or if that threshold is not met.
